title: Pub lobby attacks visa cuts in viral AI video
key_facts: The Australian Hotels Association (AHA) released a new advertisement about the knock-on effects of migration cuts.
In the ad a man presses a button to 'run Australia without migrant workers'; baristas and bar staff walk out, an aged-care worker leaves a lonely man, and a boy asks for the last $47 apple.
AHA chief executive Stephen Ferguson told 7NEWS no party is talking about the effect of losing migrant workers on hospitals, aged care, abattoirs and fruit picking.
Labor, the Coalition and One Nation all propose cutting immigration; One Nation plans a cut of 750,000 over three years.
The Mercury's headline calls it a viral AI video; the 7NEWS text read does not say how the ad was made.
quote_evidence: It paints a humorous picture of the grim "knock-on effects" that the Australian Hotels Association says "no one is talking about".
"Every Australian business wants to hire Australians first. But where we don't have those workers, we've got to look to people from overseas."
A boy asks his dad if he can have the last $47 apple rotting in a supermarket.
why_it_matters_hint: Industry lobbying with a satirical ad in the middle of an immigration-cut debate.
notes: The Mercury page blocked (403). 7NEWS covers what appears to be the same ad from the AHA (the Mercury names Hospitality Tasmania, the Tasmanian branch is assumed, not confirmed). 7NEWS does not say the ad is AI-made; only the Mercury headline does.
